UGA.note: Only Bank of Uganda monthly mobile money data and its Statistical Abstract are cited; central bank statistics are other, not administrative-record statistics from a named source.
Bank of Uganda publishes mobile money data but the document does not say it licenses providers or oversees a switch.

facts.fact: The article says that under the National Payment Systems Act an issuer must warn a customer before a mobile money wallet turns dormant, block it and notify the customer within five working days with reactivation steps, and the holder can claim the balance within seven years of its transfer to Bank of Uganda.

UGA.note: Outstanding remittances figure given without a channel or corridor.
Nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: The article describes the National Payment Systems Act as setting in-force rules on inactive and dormant mobile money wallets: 90 days without a transaction is inactive, nine months dormant, with issuer warnings, blocking, closure and transfer of balances to Bank of Uganda.
The article says the 2023 FinScope survey found 64 percent of Ugandan adults used a mobile money provider, up from 56 percent in 2018.

Bank of Uganda data cited by the Daily Monitor show 62.12 million registered mobile money accounts, 39.10 million active in the prior 90 days, and 911 million transactions worth Shs37.18 trillion in September 2026.

UGA.note: Nothing on tax or fee payment.
